summary:
Long-duration space missions expose astronauts to unique health challenges, including microgravity, radiation, isolation, and limited access to immediate medical support. InstantPulse is an interactive, web-based astronaut health and wellness monitoring prototype designed to bring essential health information, daily observations, and mission-support tools into one accessible platform.

The system enables astronauts to record vital signs, establish personal health baselines, and visualize changes over time. Its interactive body explorer, symptom guide, hydration tracker, mental wellness check-ins, cognitive reaction-time exercises, and physical activity logs support a more comprehensive view of crew well-being. Nutrition and space pantry modules help organize meals, monitor supplies, and track expiration dates.

A dedicated Mission Health Suite incorporates NASA-informed spaceflight research, including the five major hazards of human spaceflight, alongside educational monitoring tools and offline record-keeping capabilities.

Built using React and Supabase, InstantPulse addresses the challenge of maintaining astronaut health awareness during extended missions by consolidating multiple monitoring and wellness functions into a single, user-friendly interface. It demonstrates a potential approach to supporting crew independence, organized health records, and informed decision-making beyond Earth.
details:
The Challenge

As humanity prepares for longer missions to the Moon and Mars, astronaut health becomes increasingly complex. Microgravity, radiation, isolation, communication delays, and limited medical resources create a need for greater crew self-sufficiency.

Our Solution

InstantPulse is an interactive, research-informed astronaut health and wellness platform that integrates physical, psychological, cognitive, and mission-related monitoring into one accessible digital environment.

Astronauts can record vital signs, establish personalized health baselines, visualize long-term trends, and explore health indicators through an interactive Body Explorer.

What Makes InstantPulse Different?

Its standout innovation is the Mission Health Suite, which extends beyond traditional physiological monitoring:

  • MindPulse: Tracks voluntary mood, stress, loneliness, fatigue, and sleep check-ins, recognizing the psychological challenges of isolation and confinement.
  • Cognitive Readiness: Provides interactive reaction-time exercises and performance history, encouraging awareness of cognitive practice patterns.
  • Mission Health Co-Pilot: Consolidates selected physical, psychological, cognitive, and environmental observations into one convenient overview.
  • Hydration, Nutrition and Space Pantry: Supports daily fluid logging, meal tracking, food-supply management, and expiry-date awareness.
  • Exercise and Space Hazards: Helps astronauts document physical activity and understand the five major hazards of human spaceflight.

Scientific Foundation

The platform's educational content and design priorities draw on NASA's Human Research Program, NASA Johnson Space Center nutrition research, and NASA exercise countermeasure research. Relevant international research from ESA, CSA, and JAXA provides further scientific context for astronaut mental wellness, physiological monitoring, and food systems.

Technology and Design

Built using React, JavaScript, Vite, CSS, and Supabase PostgreSQL, InstantPulse combines an interactive frontend with cloud-backed data services and local browser storage. The source code is hosted on GitHub, and the application is deployed through Vercel.

The design prioritizes simple navigation, personal baseline comparisons, accessible records, limited-connectivity consideration.

Intended Impact

InstantPulse explores how one unified platform could reduce the effort of organizing mission-health information while supporting consistent wellness routines, personal awareness, and greater independence during extended space missions.
